source.note: Dark scheme (:root) is canonical; -light tokens are the prefers-color-scheme: light overrides of the same CSS custom properties.

headline.purpose: Section heads (Signal path, Speakers, Sync, Settings, Doctor, Activity) on a baseline hairline; 18 px is the largest text on the page.

brand.purpose: The product name in the top bar; 16 px, the one size off the 12 / 13 / 15 / 18 ramp, kept below the section headlines.

title.purpose: Speaker names, found-device names and signal path node titles.

body.purpose: Descriptive copy and setting labels (500); the whole page inherits tabular numerals from here.

small.purpose: The working size: facts, leads (68ch max), control labels and readouts, node subtitles, hints, ruler lane names, doctor checks, banners, toast body. Emphasis inside small is weight 600.

label.purpose: Chips, trim chips, status pips, the sink line, ruler axis labels, lane values and legend.

mono.purpose: The activity log; inline code and kbd at 0.9em of their context.

shadows.name: toast
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system, on the fixed toast (--shadow, dark scheme).

shadows.name: toast-light
shadows.purpose: The same toast shadow in the light scheme.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The one easing (--ease) for every transition.

motion.name: dur-state
motion.purpose: Background, border and colour changes on buttons, the switch and path nodes (--dur).

motion.name: dur-sweep
motion.purpose: The signal path filling from hairline to colour; staggered 0 / 80 / 160 / 240 ms (main links, trunk, branch stub, branch link). Runs only when the output flips from down to up, never on page load.

motion.name: dur-toast
motion.purpose: Toast fade and 8 px rise, in and out.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The 12 px job spinner; 1.5 s under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every transition is removed and the spinner slows; the path switches on without a sweep.

breakpoints.name: ruler-stack
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: the ruler track drops to its own row; the toast spans the width with 16 px insets.

breakpoints.name: facts-two-col
breakpoints.purpose: From: the status facts take two columns.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: 16 px gutters, 26 px section gaps, static wrapping bar with full-width actions, master control full width.

breakpoints.name: path-horizontal
breakpoints.purpose: From: the signal path becomes a five-column horizontal chain.

breakpoints.name: bar-wrap
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: the top bar may wrap.

breakpoints.name: two-column
breakpoints.purpose: From: main becomes a 7:5 two-column grid; status strip, signal path and activity span both.

components.name: Toast
components.description: The only shadowed element: a fixed notice 18 px from the bottom-right (relative here so it renders in place) with an optional spinner while a job runs, a 600 title, a quiet close and a muted body; enters by fading and rising 8 px over 180 ms.
components.html:

narrative.overview:
Soundscape's dashboard is a control surface for one person at home, laptop on the table between the speakers, lights low. The system is built for that scene first: a warm graphite ground under a deeper tinted bar, warm-white ink, and a single cobalt accent that marks what is alive, what is selected and what has focus. The light scheme keeps the same logic on a cool near-white ground. Everything else on the page is either a measurement or a control, and the colour vocabulary is sized to exactly that: six series hues that belong to speakers, three state colours that belong to conditions, nothing decorative.

Density is high and the tone is calm. One system sans on a 15 px root carries five sizes; headings are sentence case at weight 600 and never shout; every number sits in tabular figures so readouts and trims hold still while they change. Surfaces are flat and separated by 1 px hairlines and one tonal step; the only shadow on the page belongs to the toast. State is drawn as a border or ink colour change over a 200 ms ease, never as a glow, a fill or a lift.

The page refuses the dashboard default. There is no sidebar, no grid of identical metric cards, and no card nested in a panel under a tracked uppercase label. It leads with the live signal path (your apps, the Soundscape mix, a fan of branches into speaker nodes) and with the arrival ruler, the page's one signature move, where each speaker's measured arrival and its position after delay sit on a shared millisecond axis.
keyCharacteristics: Dark first, two schemes: warm graphite with a deeper bar; cool white in light with the same tonal logic.
One accent, cobalt, in two shades of one hue: `cobalt` for lines, focus, selection and the live chip; `cobalt-deep` for the filled primary action and switches.
Six series hues used only as data colour; green, amber and red only on state, always beside a word.
One system sans, five sizes on a 15 px root, sentence case everywhere, tabular numerals on the whole page.
Flat surfaces, 1 px hairlines, 10 px surface radius, 7 px control radius, a single shadow on the toast.
One authored motion: the signal path sweeps on (480 ms, staggered) only when the output comes up, never on load.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only hue that means Soundscape: primary action, selection, focus, caret and the live path. It comes in two shades of one hue and never a second hue; filled controls take `cobalt-deep`, everything drawn as a line takes `cobalt`.

rules.name: The Data Colour Rule
rules.body: The six series hues colour data and nothing else: a speaker's dot, slider, branch, set trim chip and ruler marks. They never colour a button, a heading, a card border or a surface.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only to state a condition, on text, a pip, a border or a doctor icon, and always next to the word for it (connected, headset mode, not connected). They are never decoration and never the only carrier.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number on the page is set in tabular figures and keeps its unit in the same run of text (12.0 ms, 48 kHz, 100%). Numbers that move never move their neighbours.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Nothing is uppercased or letter-spaced. There are no eyebrows or kickers; a heading carries its own weight, and a label is a muted-ink word at 12 or 13 px beside its value.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The toast is the only element that casts a shadow. Everything else is separated by a 1 px hairline or a tonal step.

rules.name: The Border Carries State Rule
rules.body: A change of state changes a border colour or an ink colour, never a shadow, a weight or a fill, so a lit node and a resting node are the same shape in the same place.

dos: Do set every number in tabular figures and keep its unit in the same run of text (`12.0 ms`, `48 kHz`, `100%`).
Do carry a state change as a border or ink colour over the 200 ms ease: cobalt when live, amber for headset mode, red for a fault.
Do bind a speaker's series hue once as `--c` on its card, branch and lane so its dot, slider, link, trim chip and ruler marks agree.
Do separate rows and sections with 1 px hairlines and lead each region with its live state before its controls.
Do write in sentence case with plain words: 18 px / 600 section heads, 13 px muted-ink labels, one primary button per region.
Do pair every colour-coded state with its word (connected, headset mode, not connected) so colour is never the only carrier.
Do keep one column below 960 px, stack the signal path below 760 px and drop the ruler track under its label at 560 px and below.
donts: Don't nest a card inside a panel or box a section; a section head is a heading on a baseline hairline.
Don't add a sidebar or a grid of identical metric cards; the page leads with the signal path and the ruler.
Don't use the series hues on buttons, headings, card borders or surfaces, or cobalt on data.
Don't put a shadow on cards, nodes, the bar or menus; the toast carries the only shadow.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; the two cobalt shades are the whole accent.
Don't uppercase or letter-space a label, and don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't paint gradients on surfaces or text; the only gradient is the hard two-stop edge that sweeps a signal line on.
Don't animate on page load; the signal path sweeps only when the output comes up, and not under reduced motion.
